title: kate-core: keep a curly apostrophe inside a word move
summary: Word right treats U+2019 as part of the word. An ASCII apostrophe stays part of the word. The test goes in the existing movement tests module.

lane.reason: A local Qwen3.8 coder model with 27B parameters on the owner Mac codes this packet. The change is one file and stays under about 60 lines.

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: movement.rs has one test module named tests. Add the new test function at the end of that module, before its closing brace. Do not write a second mod tests. Change only is_word_char. The body is one expression: ch.is_alphanumeric() || ch == '_' || ch == '\'' || ch == '\u{2019}'. Do not nest an if inside an if. Do not write two if arms that return the same value. Combine them with ||. That is clippy::if_same_then_else. Do not touch is_in_word, is_default_delimiter, kind_of, word_next, word_prev, cursor_forward, cursor_back, or move_selection. The existing tests an_apostrophe_stays_inside_the_word and word_right_from_an_apostrophe_stays_in_the_word stay green. Do not rewrite their assertions. The test word_right_crosses_a_curly_apostrophe uses TextBuffer::from_str of don, U+2019, and t. move_selection of WordRight from Selection::caret of Offset(0) with Extend::No and ctx() has head Offset(5). The same move from Offset(3) has head Offset(5). Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip. Keep the change under about 60 lines. Run the full test module named in the commands, not only the new test.

regression_tests.name: movement::tests::word_right_crosses_a_curly_apostrophe
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main. Word right from the start of don plus U+2019 plus t stops at Offset(3). After the change the caret is Offset(5). The same move from Offset(3) also lands on Offset(5).
